coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED. (1) Wikipedia's 2010 Auburn Tigers football team page — a 12-name coaching-staff box; quotes verified verbatim against the rendered page (note the en dashes). (2) Auburn's own athletics site as archived on the Wayback Machine at 2010-12-27, two weeks before the BCS title game: https://web.archive.org/web/20101227182251/http://www.auburntigers.com/sports/m-footbl/mtt/aub-m-footbl-mtt.html — a 20-name Coaches list covering the ten on-field coaches plus operations, video, strength, chaplain and medical staff. On that page the name and the title live in adjacent cells of one table row; stripping tags yields the contiguous "Name - Title" strings quoted here, so a plain-text extraction will match, but a markdown extraction that renders the name as a link may not. (3) The 2010 Auburn Football Media Guide, scanned at the Internet Archive (https://archive.org/details/auburn-football-2010-media-guide), whose "Football Support Staff", "Strength & Conditioning Staff" and "Medical Staff" spreads (printed pages 77-84) are the only source for roughly half this list. (4) Auburn's current site, 2010 season archive (https://auburntigers.com/sports/football/roster/season/2010), which lists the ten on-field coaches but flattens every title to "Assistant Coach". (5) Present-day staff bios at SMU and Auburn for verbatim confirmation of Rhett Lashlee's and Travis Williams' 2010 roles.

QUOTE QUALITY CAVEAT — READ BEFORE STRING-MATCHING. The media guide sets every staffer's surname in a heavy distressed display face, which the Internet Archive OCR either mangles or drops entirely. As a result no single line of the OCR text file carries both a name and a title for these people. Where a title string is contiguous and verbatim in the OCR text file I have quoted it and named the person in the note; where even that failed (Brad Rapacz) I set quote to "" per instructions. I resolved every mangled surname by rendering the PDF pages to images and reading them directly, so the names here are confirmed by eye against the printed page, not guessed: Eliah Drinkwitz, Erik Link, T.J. Graham, Ryan Russell, Clark Pearson and Kirk Nielson were all unrecoverable from OCR alone. Page images are at https://archive.org/download/auburn-football-2010-media-guide/page/n{N}_w1600.jpg where N is the PDF page index minus one (support staff run n73-n80).

TIMING. The media guide is a preseason publication (summer 2010), so it documents the staff as constituted entering the season; the Wayback capture of the coaches list is from Dec. 27, 2010, i.e. after the SEC Championship Game and before the Jan. 10, 2011 BCS title game. Both bracket the championship, and I found no evidence of any arrival or departure between them, so no midseason_note is set on anyone. The well-known departures from this staff (Ted Roof to Central Florida, Jeff Grimes to Virginia Tech, Curtis Luper to TCU) all came after the title game. I did search for mid-2010 staff changes and found none, but that search was not exhaustive and a low-profile QC or GA turnover could have escaped it.

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT. Individual staff bio pages on the 2010 auburntigers.com (bolt_wayne00.html, fountain_scott00.html, etc.) were linked from the roster page but are not in the Wayback Machine, so no per-person primary web page exists for the support staff. I found no archived athletics-department staff directory from fall 2010 that would add football names. Categories almost certainly larger than what is documented here: student assistants and undergraduate managers (none are listed anywhere I could find), equipment and video interns, and athletic training graduate assistants — Joe-Joe Petrone's own bio says he oversees "12 certified full-time staff and 11 certified graduate assistants" across the whole department, and only three football trainers plus Petrone are named. Auburn also carried no "analyst" title in this era, which is why that category is empty; the analyst-equivalent work sat under the quality control and graduate assistant titles listed above.

JUDGMENT CALLS. Chad Lunsford's title differs between sources — "Football Operations Video Coordinator" on the website versus "Football Operations Director of Scouting" in the media guide; I used the website wording as the role and flagged the other in his note. Gus Malzahn, Trooper Taylor, Curtis Luper, Phillip Lolley and Tommy Thigpen also have two documented wordings each, both cited. I included Kirk Sampson, Matt Crouch, Brad Gust and Bob Grant (media relations) and Jeremy Roberts (athletic operational support) because the media guide prints them on its "Football Support Staff" page, but they are athletics-department employees serving football rather than football-only staff — downstream ring logic may want to treat them differently. I excluded athletics director Jay Jacobs and university president Jay Gogue, who appear in the guide on a separate administration spread, not the football staff pages. Every one of the 46 rows above traces to a source I actually fetched and read; nothing is inferred from background knowledge.
